1.1: 1.1 There was. On account of the fewness of spiritual teachers to whom authority of judging is given, there was a famine of the word of God, when even the law was corrupted by Jewish traditions. And a man went, RABANUS. Christ, namely, born in Bethlehem of Judah visited the pilgrimage of this world, with his wife, that is the Church, and with two sons, the two orders of prophets and apostles who by the blood of Christ were freed from the slavery of sin. A man went. RABANUS. Whom some understand as the Decalogue of the law, and his wife the synagogue, and the two sons, the royal honor and the priestly: who acquired to themselves not only in the nation of the Jews but also the union of proselytes, as was done in the time of David, and Solomon and others.
1.2: 1.2 Mahalon. Who from the window or from the beginning. This is the chorus of prophets through whom from the window first the light of faith went forth into the world: who were also the first preachers of the true light, that is Christ. Chelion, consummation. These are the apostles who led the riddles of the prophets to the consummation of full understanding. These deservedly are Ephrathites and born of Bethlehem of Judah: who filled with heavenly bread by the preaching of the Gospel gathered the fruit of preaching. For Ephrathite is interpreted fruitful, Bethlehem house of bread, Judah confession, whence: Give them your hand. Likewise, Going preach the Gospel of the kingdom of God. And elsewhere: I have chosen you from the world that you go and bring forth fruit, Mark 6, 16; John 16.
1.4: 1.4 Ruth. She is interpreted seeing or hastening, or failing: in which the obedience and credulity of the Gentiles is designated, of whom it is said: A people which I knew not has served me, etc. And elsewhere: Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God, Psalm 67. The two peoples were called therefore by holy preachers to the fellowship of the faith and of the elect of God, that from diverse flocks there might be one fold.
1.5: 1.5 They died. After the perfection of pious labor, they migrated from the exile of this world to the heavenly kingdoms, that, the commandment of the Decalogue fulfilled, they might receive the penny of beatitude.
1.7: 1.7 She went out, etc., both. The Church zealously strives to bring the peoples whom the Apostles and prophets instructed in their time to the unity of faith and the fellowship of Christian religion: which she learned by Scripture's report, that the just man will not be forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread, which comes down from heaven, Psalm 36.
1.8: 1.8 Go to the house. The Church acts not indiscreetly, nor indiscriminately receives any, whence: Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God, 1 John 4. These words can fit the synagogue, which draws back to the faith of Christ those who come, and especially this, that overcome by the truth she knows herself too weak to bear: Return, my daughters.
1.11: 1.11 Do I yet. RABANUS. The voice of the synagogue confessing the truth and not silent about the guilt that came upon her, who, left by her husband, that is David: and deprived of sons, that is kings and princes, confesses herself barren and weak to conceive sons for God after the coming of Christ.
1.14: 1.14 Lifted up. By these women, one of whom with grief and weeping departs from her mother-in-law, the other clings with obstinate mind, believers are signified: of whom some, having received the grace of baptism and fellowship, fall back into former errors, whom Orpah signifies: who returned to her gods; others with fixed counsel obtain the grace received, whom Ruth signifies.
1.16: 1.16 Whithersoever. So the Church called from the Gentiles, leaving the country, that is idolatry abandoned, carnal conversation and desires, professes that her God is he in whom the saints believed, and that she will go where the flesh of Christ ascended, and suffer for his name in this world unto death, and with the people of the saints and prophets and patriarchs; whence: Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people, Romans 15.
1.18: 1.18 Seeing. The Gentile people with obstinate mind follow the preachers into the holy land, and into the city of God, Bethlehem, where it is prepared to receive the bridegroom born of the stock of Abraham, in whom all nations or tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
1.20: 1.20 Call me not. The synagogue acknowledges her calamity, which she deservedly suffers after the coming of Christ: and shuns being called beautiful, because she sees the times of her prosperity ending. When first. That is when the law turned the order of its incarnation to the mystery of the passion of Christ. For the barley harvest expresses the time of the Lord's passion, which occurred in the month of new things, that is, the first month. Well therefore at that time they come to Bethlehem, when the law preaches Christ, whom it teaches born in Bethlehem, slain at the pasch, that is in the month of new things. The holy Church also labors with all effort to imbue those she calls to the faith with the merit of the incarnation, passion, resurrection. The barley harvest expresses the credulity of the Jews: who, the sacrament of the passion completed, the apostles preaching, first come to the faith. Who elsewhere are read to be fed by the Lord with five barley loaves.
2.3: 2.3 It happened. Because holy Church belongs to Christ, whose bride and body she is. Of whom it is said: The Lord is my strength and my praise, Psalm 117. And elsewhere: The Lord strong and mighty. The Lord mighty in battle, Psalm 23. He is the kinsman of Elimelech, who born of Bethlehem and the stock of David, has testimony from the law and prophets. He brought words of salvation and peace to his family, at whose nativity the angels sang, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth, etc., Luke 2. To whom coming into Jerusalem the crowd met and cried, saying: Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord, Matthew 21.
2.7: 2.7 And she asked. Because holy Church perseveres in the field of divine reading after the reapers and preachers, gathering the mysteries of the Scriptures, to record in the bosom of her mind the testimonies and examples of virtues. Or that field is the discipline of heavenly study, the harvest spiritual understanding; the reapers, preachers; the remaining ears, sentences of the Scriptures, which hidden much by mystery, remain as if fuller for the exercise of him who meditates. The Gentile people therefore ardently desire ecclesiastical discipline, that they may be admitted to meditation of the divine law and fellowship of the saints, and be refreshed by the documents or examples of the saints.
2.8: 2.8 Go not. As if to say: Depart not from the state of faith, follow not the errors of heretics or schismatics: but rather join the holy souls, that you may reap the holy Scriptures, by meditating, and fulfilling in work; and draw the draught of divine wisdom from the books of the two Testaments whence the servants, that is, the saints drink, and drink it yourself.
2.10: 2.10 Who falling on her face. The Church of the Gentiles gives thanks to the Savior, who deigned to look upon her. To whom he answered: that it pleased him that, her husband being dead, that is the devil, she left idolatrous parents, and the land of her birth, that is carnal desires, and joined herself to the people of the saints, who was before unknown to her when she followed the cupidity of the old man.
2.13: 2.13 Let me find, etc. Note the humility of the Gentile Church, which knows herself unequal to so great grace, nor dares to compare herself to the primitive Church; whence she says: For the whelps also eat of the crumbs, etc. And elsewhere: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my servant shall be healed, Matthew 8.
2.14: 2.14 At the time. The hour of eating was when it was said to the apostles: Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Matthew 16. For it was said by the Lord: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, Matthew 10. Dip your morsel. The law, namely, which long meditated and persevering in the former people, corrupted by the conditions or traditions of the Pharisees, lost its native savor. In this the Church dips the morsel, that is, says the mystery of the incarnation of Christ is in the Old Testament, and therefore believes more firmly, because she knows it was prefigured long before.
2.16: 2.16 Of your own. Note the humility of the master of the house, who not only permits the left-over ears of testimonies to be gathered, but even imparts handfuls of knowledge by spontaneous largesse. Throw down of your own hands, etc. Because he does not despise the infirmity of the Gentile people, nor reproach their former errors, but by sagacity of zeal leads them to edification.
2.17: 2.17 About an ephi. When in reading through the confession of the holy Trinity she learns the Catholic faith. In the measure ephi, which contains three measures, is signified the one substance of the Godhead, and the property of the three persons.
2.18: 2.18 Which carrying. Because she shows her faith to the mother Church. Or the Church shows the synagogue the grace which she received by the gift of her Spouse, to provoke her to the faith. She gave her. My heart has uttered a good word, namely of the fullness of the heart the food of preaching. Blessed. The synagogue, the Church of the Gentiles preaching, recognizes the goodness and power of the Lord, and the strength of her protector: and at last, truth compelling, blesses the name of the Lord, who has kept grace for the dead which he offered to the living.
2.20: 2.20 Kinsman. Mother Church recognizes the kinsman by the gratuitous benefits conferred on the Gentile people, and at the hearing of the name remembers the ancient benefits; whence: I remembered the days of old, I meditated on all your works, Psalm 142.
2.21: 2.21 He commanded me. Because Christ commands all coming to him that they be joined rather with his faithful ones for the harvest of the spiritual crop, than with strangers, to which persuasion the mother-in-law consents, saying: It is better, daughter; this as good and profitable the Synagogue cannot deny.
2.23: 2.23 Until the wheat. That is, so long she clings to the teachers in meditation of the Scriptures, until she stores the knowledge of the Old and New Testament in the cell of her heart: whence she might have sufficient food for the soul.
3.2: 3.2 The threshing floor. The synagogue of the Jews where the barley of the law is stored: this Christ winnows, when preaching the Gospel on the threshing floor, he threshes the counsels and wills of each toward himself; whence: But Jesus did not trust himself to them, for that he knew all men, and because he needed not that any should bear witness of man, John 2.
3.3: 3.3 Be not known. Because the faith of the Gentile Church did not appear before Christ had fulfilled the mystery of his incarnation, when bodily living among men he used food and drink, and at last supping with his disciples shared with them the sacraments of his body and blood. The mystery of the dispensation having been fulfilled, the Church of Christ from the Gentiles came confidently to the faith.
3.4: 3.4 Uncover, etc. What he says: Acknowledge Christ suffered for you, and come with devout mind, unveil the covering of the letter of the Old Testament in which the sacrament of the incarnation of Christ is hidden; and when you have learned thence salvation promised to you, flee humbly to his help, that you may remain there at all times.
3.7: 3.7 The heap. The testimonies of the Scriptures; whence: The Son of man goes as it is written of him, Matthew 26. Or near the companies of faithful souls which by his death he recalled from hell. To this bed the Church hastened, and the mantle uncovered, etc.
3.12: 3.12 But there is another nearer than I. John the Baptist who was thought to be the Christ, but did not usurp the name of bridegroom, but reserved it to Christ, saying: He that has the bride is the bridegroom, etc. He is nearer, because born earlier in the world. Or this kinsman is the decalogue of the law, which seemed nearer to the Synagogue than the Gospel, because given specially to that people and earlier in time.
3.14: 3.14 She rose up therefore before. Because before the Jews imbued with the teaching of the law knew the rights of their nature, the Church of the Gentiles, shaking off the sleep of her sluggishness, rose at the dawn of newborn faith, and hastened to the grace of Christ.
4.1: 4.1 Turn aside. Because Christ saw the law established for the Jews temporally: and commanded it to turn aside to him: because he bent it to testify the mystery of his dispensation. Otherwise: he saw the kinsman pass by, when he saw the coming of his forerunner hastening after the manner of human life, and mercifully turned him to the office of forerunner. He spoke. Fittingly he offered to the lawyers a part of the field of Naomi to buy, when he showed to the masters of the Synagogue the part of the people who remained, grace now appearing, for salvation, that they might acknowledge their weakness, and commit to the true physician what they could not do, whence to the lepers it is said: Go, show yourselves to the priests, Luke 17., and as they went they were cleansed.
4.5: 4.5 To raise up. It signifies no other possession of the people than the union of the Church in marriage with Christ, who raised up the ancient name of son of God which the saints had at the beginning; whence: The sons of God seeing, etc., and Luke says: Adam the son of God, whom also in the Church of the Gentiles he raised up by the grace of God; whence: He gave them power to become sons of God, etc. This name among the nations the decalogue of the law could not raise up. But if you refer this to John the Baptist, you will find him yielding to the right of kinship, and saying: I baptize with water: but there has stood one in the midst of you whom you know not: the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose. And elsewhere: I am not the Christ: but am sent before him. He that has the bride, is the bridegroom. The law also yields to the Gospel: For the law entered in that sin might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did more abound. There is indeed a rejection of the preceding commandment on account of its weakness: but the introduction of a better hope by which we draw near to God is by Jesus Christ.
4.8: 4.8 To loose. The shoe is the veil of the mysteries. The law loosed the shoe from its foot, and gave it to Christ, because it could not make the sacraments manifest through the masters of the people, but reserved this to be done by Christ. John therefore claimed the shoe not for himself but for Christ, because he understood the bride belongs to Christ alone; whence he says: I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his shoe.
4.9: 4.9 Witnesses. So Christ has sufficient witnesses from both Testaments, because the Gentile people, whom the decalogue now finished could not spiritually make fruitful, he himself made fruitful with the seed of the word of God, possessing all things which the saints before and after have had.
4.11: 4.11 And the elders. ISIDORE. The blessing of the ten elders shows that in the name of Jesus all nations are to be blessed. For iota among the Greeks signifies ten, which in the name of Jesus is the first letter. The Lord make this. He invokes prosperity on the Church of the Gentiles, that she may receive the grace of fruitfulness which the first parents of the Israelites had. Rachel. Having by the hope of inward contemplation an inward understanding of truth. Whence, Rachel fair of face, and beautiful in appearance, whom every pious zealous man loves, and for her serves Laban, who is interpreted whitening, which he compares to the grace of God who says: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made white as snow, Isaiah 1. Leah. The action of this life in which we live is laborious from faith, and uncertain, by what outcome it comes to the profit of those we wish to advise. She is Leah, the first wife of Jacob, who is recorded to have had weak eyes.
4.12: 4.12 Perez, etc. Who held the grace of the Gentile people, and in the birth preceded the brother who had put out his hand first, for Israel first put out the hand in the work of the law, and drew it back polluted with the blood of the prophets and of Christ himself. Afterward, however, the people of the Gentiles broke forth, that the last might be first, and the first last, Matthew 20. Tamar also is interpreted changing or bitterness. For the Church of the Gentiles both in name and habit, which was in idolatry foul and bitter, in penance becomes sweet and beautiful.
4.13: 4.13 That she might conceive and bear. Always the Church is made fruitful by the gift of the Holy Spirit, and, others departing to perpetual light, others will succeed, that the Christian name may remain forever and the most holy mother of a new offspring in her old age may have consolation. As patriarchs and prophets departed, evangelists and apostles succeeded, whence: Instead of your fathers sons are born to you.
4.15: 4.15 For of the daughter-in-law. The daughter-in-law of the synagogue is the Gentile Church who married Christ born of the synagogue. Whom she, namely, could not bring forth through the law, she carried hidden under a veil, figured in the mystery of prophecy received, and discharged the office of nurse, because she lacked the privilege of mother. Much better to you, etc. The multitude, namely, of those who in the Old Testament nourished the doctrine of the law, who indeed believed not the word of the Lord and sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, and at length killed Christ and persecuted the apostles.
4.16: 4.16 And nurse. The spiritual lineage of generation is shown. For Obed is interpreted Servile. Jesse, in the sun a sacrifice or incense; David, strong of hand or desirable. For he who strenuously serves God offers him an acceptable sacrifice and most sweet incense of odor by works of virtue and zeal of prayer. And thus strengthened by faith and devotion he is desirable and pleases God.
4.17: 4.17 Neighbors. The heavenly virtues, who rejoice in the fruitfulness of the Church, and call his name Obed, that is serving, whom they desire to serve with them the heavenly King.
4.18: 4.18 These are. There are ten generations from the son of Judah to David. Whence you know that the intention of the whole divine law tends to Christ, who was born of the seed of David, that it may preach his coming and manifest the perfection of the law in him: For Christ is the end of the law unto justice to every one that believes, Romans 10. Before the law therefore Jacob said of the incarnation of Christ: The scepter shall not be taken away from Judah, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent. To David, however, because Christ is of the seed of Judah, it was said: Of the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne. It is plain therefore that the oracles also of the prophets and patriarchs pertain to the dispensation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
